first_glance_test: A brand-new user sees a static mathematics lecture slide demonstrating polynomial-kernel expansion. No interactive actions are offered on screen. The screen appears to offer only one "action": read the proof. Given the injected VIEW purpose (SVM/kernels/QP lecture frame), the focal point should be the final equality proving the kernel trick, and it does win the eye via the bottom-left 144 result and the trailing red arrow. Nothing is confusing or demands study beyond normal parsing of math notation.

Color coding is consistent and purposeful: blue for vectors, red for operators/results, black for body math (both panels, throughout).
Large, legible math type; no cramped notation or microtext (both panels, all equations).

no changes — the two-panel theory/example stack is the correct structure for a lecture frame; no reorganisation is needed or visible.
[out-of-scope] no new features or panes are warranted; the screen already fulfills its single purpose.
